paper_sections.title: First Symptoms and Neurocognitive Correlates of Behavioral Variant Frontotemporal Dementia
Assessment of neuroanatomical markers: whole-brain and regions of interest (ROI) analyses
Statistical analyses at second stage measures
Correlations between neuropsychological measures and ROIs in each group

description.value: The study examined whether the first behavioral symptom of bvFTD, apathy or disinhibition, is associated with later neuropsychological and neuroanatomical profiles and whether these measures distinguish the two patient subgroups.

design.value: Cross-sectional comparison of healthy controls and two bvFTD patient groups defined retrospectively by their first symptom, with neuropsychological testing, 3T structural MRI voxel-based morphometry, brain-behavior correlations, and multivariate classification analyses conducted around three years after disease debut.

source_definition.value: FrSBe scores were used as a subjective measure of apathy.
A global score of disinhibition was based on scores of both subjective and objective indexes used to assess disinhibition; FrSBe scores and Hayling Test scores were used.

task_description.value: Neuroanatomical correlates were assessed using 3T structural images and voxel-based morphometry.

instrument.value: Philips Achieva 3T scanner with a 16-channel SENSE antenna

description.value: The anatomical and 3D T1-weighted images had TR = 7.9, TE = 3.8, ACQ matrix 220×220 pixels, voxel size 0.5×0.5×0.5 mm, and 310 sections.

T1-weighted images were normalized to stereotaxic space using the DARTEL algorithm, segmented into WM and GM and non-brain voxels, modulated to correct volume changes by Jacobian determinants, and smoothed with an isotropic Gaussian kernel of 8-mm full-width at half maximum.

software.value: VBM8 in the Statistical Parametric Mapping 8 package (SPM8)

steps.value: Each image was inspected for artifacts.
The T1-weighted images were normalized to the same stereotaxic space generated from the complete data set using the DARTEL algorithm.
The images were segmented into WM and GM and non-brain voxels (CSF, skull).
All images were modulated to correct volume changes by Jacobian determinants.
Images were smoothed by convolution with an isotropic Gaussian kernel of 8-mm full-width at half maximum.

model_settings.value: Whole-brain analyses and ROI analyses comparing AbvFTD, DbvFTD, and healthy controls; analyses controlled for global intracranial volume, age, gender, and length of disease duration. Whole-brain analyses were corrected with FDR at 0.001 and ROI analyses with FDR at 0.05.
A one-way ANOVA was used to assess differences in neuropsychological measures between groups of patients, and one-way ANOVA and chi square tests were used for categorical demographic variables.
Multiple correlations between VBM scores in ROIs and standardized neuropsychological measures, with Sidak correction.

estimator.value: Pearson correlation coefficient with Sidak correction

model_settings.value: Two models were used: one including significant neuropsychological measures and neuroanatomical variables, and one including only significant neuroanatomical variables. A final stepwise discriminant analysis was performed at the 5% level.

SVM models used recursive feature elimination, optimization of γ and C, and 10-fold cross-validation. Models included neuropsychological and ROI variables, whole-brain anatomical variables, or ROI variables alone.

name.value: Whole brain analysis comparing AbvFTD with healthy controls

model_representation_notes.value: controlling for global intracranial volume, age, gender and length of disease duration

interpretations.value: The AbvFTD group showed reduced VBM values in R DLPFC, R-L OFC, R-L ACC, and R-L Caud.

name.value: Whole brain analysis comparing DbvFTD with healthy controls

model_representation_notes.value: controlling for global intracranial volume, age, gender and length of disease duration

interpretations.value: DbvFTD showed reduced VBM values in more areas, including the R DLPFC, R OFC, R-L ACC, L STG, R-L Caud, medial frontal regions, and bilateral insula.
The AbvFTD > DbvFTD contrast showed major atrophy for the apathetic group in the R DLPFC, Left precuneus, Right Angular Gyrus, and L Caudate.
The DbvFTD > AbvFTD contrast reflected major brain atrophy for the disinhibited group in R-L OFC, R FM, R DLPFC, L STG, R-L ACC, and Left and Right Temporal Middle.
